title: Weather and Commodities: Winter Outlook Hinges on El-Niño | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF argues an unprecedentedly strong El Niño is the dominant predictor for the 2026-27 Northern Hemisphere winter, pointing to a mild US and Europe (about 1C above the 30-year average) that should ease gas and power price stress. Upside risks are Arctic cold intrusions linked to an emerging sudden stratospheric warming signal, US freeze-offs, and a late cold, low-wind spell in Europe, while rain replacing Alpine and Nordic snow could weaken European hydropower in 2027.

themes.theme: El Niño as dominant winter driver

insights.claim: BNEF views the unprecedented strength of the developing El Niño as the main meaningful predictive tool for forecasting the 2026-27 Northern Hemisphere winter.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Seasonal energy and weather-sensitive commodity positioning can be anchored to a single, unusually strong climate signal.
insights.quote: The unprecedented strength of the developing phenomenon makes it the main meaningful predictive tool for forecasting this winter.
insights.locator: The story of the weather this

insights.claim: El Niño's influence is clearest across the US (milder north, wetter south) and weaker over Europe, where Atlantic and stratospheric circulation can more easily modify its effect.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Forecast confidence, and thus the reliability of a mild-winter trade, is higher for US markets than European ones.
insights.quote: Its influence on Europe is weaker and more easily modified by Atlantic and stratospheric circulation

insights.claim: Despite the weaker linkage, El Niño's global impact is expected to keep Europe about 1 degree Celsius warmer than the 30-year average this winter.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A ~1C warm anomaly materially reduces European heating demand and gas burn.
insights.quote: El Niño’s global impact is expected to keep the continent 1 degree Celsius warmer than the 30-year average.

insights.claim: BNEF builds its winter weather scenarios from historical climate observations since 1950 combined with seasonal forecasts from major modeling centers, and tracks El Niño strength via the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
entities: International Research Institute for Climate and Society
insights.so_what: Shows the analogue-plus-model basis behind the call, useful for judging how much weight to give it.
insights.quote: BNEF compiles historical climate observations since 1950 and seasonal forecasts from major modeling centers to create weather scenarios for the current winter.

themes.theme: US gas: bearish base case, cold-snap tail

insights.claim: In the last two strongest modern El Niño events, US gas storage sat 19% and 13% above the five-year normal respectively across December-February, implying warmth should curb US gas demand this winter.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Historical analogues point to a storage surplus and bearish pressure on US natural gas prices.
insights.quote: the last two strongest El Niño events in the modern era seeing gas storage sit at 19% and 13% above the five-year normal
insights.locator: Warmth in the US should curb

insights.claim: Brief cold outbreaks and production freeze-offs remain the principal bullish risk for US gas despite the mild El Niño outlook.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Short-gas positions carry tail risk from short, sharp cold events that hit both demand and supply.
insights.quote: Yet brief cold outbreaks and freeze-offs remain the principal bullish gas risk.
insights.locator: Warmth in the US should curb

insights.claim: A wetter southern storm track should benefit California's hydropower, which supports around 10% of the state's electricity generation on average.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Stronger hydro output could displace gas-fired generation in California and soften regional power prices.
insights.quote: A wetter southern storm track favors California’s hydropower, which supports around 10% of electricity generation on average.
insights.locator: Warmth in the US should curb

themes.theme: Europe power: mild, wet, windy and bearish

insights.claim: Europe's mild, wet and windy outlook is bearish for power demand: temperatures near 1C above normal cut heating demand, stronger wind lifts renewable output, and rainfall boosts reservoirs and waterways.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Multiple supply and demand factors line up for softer European power and gas prices this winter.
insights.quote: Europe’s mild, wet and windy outlook is bearish for power demand.

insights.claim: The main European winter risk is a late cold-and-low-wind period, which would raise demand while cutting renewable supply.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A late-winter dunkelflaute-type event is the key scenario that could flip European power and gas prices higher.
insights.quote: The main risk is a late cold-and-low-wind period

insights.claim: Precipitation falling as rain instead of snow risks Europe's snowpack, so rain replacing Alpine and Nordic snow may weaken hydropower in 2027 even as it helps reservoirs this winter.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A bearish winter could set up tighter European power balances in 2027 as the snowpack buffer for hydro thins.
insights.quote: rain replacing Alpine and Nordic snow may weaken hydropower in 2027.

themes.theme: Stratospheric upside risks and price relief

insights.claim: Weakening winds in the Arctic stratosphere, which unexpectedly began emerging in late October, raise the risk of sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) events that can trigger isolated cold air outbreaks and quickly lift heating demand.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: An early SSW signal is a watch item that could abruptly reverse a mild-winter price trade.
insights.quote: Weakening winds in the Arctic stratosphere raises the risk of sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) events

insights.claim: Unseasonably warm weeks should relieve price stress in gas and power markets, offering respite amid ongoing geopolitical turmoil, though near-term predictions of Arctic cold intrusions remain an upside price risk.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Weather may offset geopolitically driven energy price pressure this winter, but with asymmetric cold-snap risk.
insights.quote: These unseasonably warm weeks should relieve price stress in gas and power markets, much-needed respite given the geopolitical turmoil.
